target_customer: Small businesses such as restaurants and bars paying vendor invoices; originally field service and delivery teams
problem: Small businesses pay supplier invoices through slow manual processes; the initial pitch addressed coordination for field and delivery teams.
business_model: B2B payments software (invoice capture and pay vendors); original logistics SaaS

founders.name: Steve Abraham
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch name him; no bio in either.

technical_complexity.rationale: Invoice parsing from photos and bank payments need OCR and payments integrations; small team scope at the time is not documented.

defensibility.rationale: No data or integration moat shown in sources; payments for restaurants was a crowded wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Unknown; no source on incumbent action or on who acquired Symple.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in February 2017 framed paying invoices as a pain for restaurants and bars, but cites no spend or complaint data.

branding.domain_note: YC lists getsymple.com, which did not resolve in this session.

identity.voice_and_tone: Venmo for Businesses framing in TechCrunch coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Little coverage beyond one TechCrunch article; the name is a respelling of simple and easily confused with other Symple products such as an unrelated symple.my.

pivots.from: Logistics platform for field service and delivery teams (YC directory description)
pivots.to: B2B invoice payments, Venmo for Businesses
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred only from differing descriptions in TechCrunch (Feb 2017) and the YC page

outcome_analysis: Symple is listed by YC as acquired, but no acquirer, date or price was found in searches. Coverage is thin: a February 2017 TechCrunch article describes a B2B invoice payments product for restaurants and bars, which differs from the logistics description on the YC page. With no funding or exit data public, the story cannot be reconstructed and the cause of the outcome is not public.
notes: Website getsymple.com did not resolve (dead or blocked). TechCrunch places Symple in YC Winter 2017 while the YC directory says Summer 2016. CB Insights reports 120K dollars seed from YC dated 2017-03 but its profile also mixes in an unrelated furniture rental business, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Searches for competitors with dates found nothing about Symple; symple.my is an unrelated company. Exit type unknown although the directory says Acquired. Completeness pass: The 120K dollar seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, also echoed by Seedtable's profile), and its profile may mix in an unrelated business. Seedtable alone says Feather bought Symple.
